items.question: How do the phases of breath relate to the seizing of time?
premises: With inhalations and retentions the power holds and seizes time.
With exhalation it completely seizes all time.
Risen with exhalation, it acts in an instant.
items.inference: The breath phases progressively master time, culminating in instantaneous total seizure through exhalation.
uncertainties: The subject of grasate/saṃgrasate is carried from the preceding context (the power).
items.plain_english: Through inhalations and retentions it holds and seizes time, but through exhalation it completely seizes all time; rising with the exhalation, it does so in an instant.

items.question: Which power is to be worshipped and what does it accomplish?
premises: The supreme will-power, named as the awakener of the three powers, is to be worshipped.
It draws in everything.
Its action shatters the support of time.
items.inference: Worship of the supreme will-power, which awakens the three powers, results in the drawing in of all and the collapse of time's foundation.
items.plain_english: The supreme will-power, by name the awakener of the three powers, is to be worshipped; it draws in all and shatters the very support of time.

items.question: How do the powers of seeing, action, and will manifest in different subjects?
premises: The powers of seeing, action, and will have been spoken of, O Shiva.
In the gross and subtle cutting of the knowable, in order, they operate.
They become the sakala and pralayākala subjects respectively.
items.inference: The three powers, operating at gross and subtle levels of knowable-division, correspond to the sakala and pralayākala states.
uncertainties: The exact mapping of gross/subtle to sakala/pralayākala is compressed in the verse.
items.plain_english: O Shiva, the powers of seeing, action, and will, when engaged in the gross and subtle cutting of the knowable, become in order the sakala and the pralayākala.

items.question: What states arise when the powers are asleep or awakened in purity?
premises: When pure but asleep, the powers become the state of the knowledge-limited subject.
When awakened, they know some divided knowables.
In that awakened state they are called mantras.
items.inference: The same pure powers yield the vijñānākala state when asleep and the mantra level when awakened to partial knowledge.
items.plain_english: When pure but asleep, the powers become the knowledge-limited state; when awakened, knowing some divided knowables, they are called mantras.

items.question: How do higher lordly subjects arise as the knowable becomes fully or partly divided?
premises: When the entire knowable is divided, the lords of mantras and great lords arise.
When the knowable is both divided and undivided, the path up to Sadāśiva arises.
This culminates in the supreme Lord.
items.inference: Degrees of division in the knowable correspond to ascending levels from mantreśas to Sadāśiva and the supreme Lord.
uncertainties: The compound suśivānto@dhvoditaḥ is read as the path arisen up to Sadāśiva.
items.plain_english: When the whole knowable is divided, the lords of mantras and the great lords arise; when it is both divided and undivided, the path up to Sadāśiva arises, culminating in the supreme Lord.

items.question: How do the powers transform as difference expands and then dissolves?
premises: As the expansion of difference dissolves, the powers gradually come to expansion.
Mutually mixed, they become the triad of tvaras.
When difference has dissolved, they move beyond that triad.
items.inference: The powers pass from differentiated expansion to a mutually mixed triad and then to a state where difference is dissolved.
uncertainties: tvarātrayaṃ refers to the triad of tvaras in the Trika system; kept as a technical term in sense.
items.plain_english: As the expansion of difference dissolves, those powers gradually expand and, mutually mixed, become the triad of tvaras; then, with difference dissolved, they go beyond it.

items.question: What forms the seat of worship and why do the powers assume it?
premises: The triad of lotuses together with unmanā functions as the seat.
The powers assume this seat.
They do so from a desire to cut off their mutual difference.
items.inference: The lotus triad and unmanā serve as the ritual seat because the powers seek to transcend their mutual differentiation.
uncertainties: The verse is syntactically compressed; the causal link is inferred from the instrumental.
items.plain_english: The triad of lotuses together with unmanā becomes the seat, as the powers take it up out of a desire to cut away their mutual difference.

items.question: Why do the divisions of power and its possessor become objects of worship?
premises: The divisions of power, its possessor, and so on come to be worshipped.
This begins from the first point where difference dissolves.
From that point each bears its own proper form.
items.inference: These divisions become worshippable because, from the threshold of dissolving difference, each manifests its own true form.
items.plain_english: Indeed, the divisions of power, its possessor, and so forth become worthy of worship, because from the very first point of the dissolution of difference each bears its own proper form.

items.question: Why is the threefoldness of these powers clearly perceived?
premises: The powers bear a threefold structure.
Their threefoldness is clearly perceived.
This clarity arises from possible impurity of the knowable and mutual mixture.
items.inference: The triadic distinction becomes evident because of the knowable's potential impurity and the powers' mutual intermixture.
items.plain_english: They bear a threefoldness, and that threefoldness of theirs is clearly perceived because of the possible impurity of the knowable and the mutual mixture they acquire.

items.question: Why is the supreme consciousness called Kālakarṣiṇī rather than threefold?
premises: Before this level the threefold state does not appear in the same clear way.
This consciousness is ready to devour the cutting of mutual difference.
Its essence is freedom alone, and so it is called Kālakarṣiṇī.
items.inference: Because it transcends triadic division by consuming difference and rests in pure freedom, consciousness is named Kālakarṣiṇī.
items.plain_english: Not arriving at a clearly threefold state as before, but ready to devour the very act of cutting mutual difference, that consciousness, whose essence is freedom alone, is declared to be Kālakarṣiṇī.

items.question: Why is the same consciousness also called Saṃkarṣiṇī among the Mothers?
premises: She draws time back into herself.
She expels time outward here.
Among these Mothers this is her true mode of being, so she is called Saṃkarṣiṇī.
items.inference: Her dual act of drawing in and projecting out time establishes her identity as Saṃkarṣiṇī among the Mothers.
items.plain_english: She again draws time back from herself and also projects it outward; therefore she is declared Saṃkarṣiṇī, and this is her true being among these Mothers.

items.question: What is the true nature and supreme reality of the Mothers and powers?
premises: True nature, being, and attainment are measured in relation to the Mothers.
This applies to the world-generating powers.
Their supreme reality is nothing but freedom.
items.inference: The ontological status of the Mothers and powers is grounded in their supreme reality, which is sheer autonomy.
uncertainties: meyo@nayā is read as 'by this measure/criterion' in a compressed doctrinal sense.
items.plain_english: True nature, being, and attainment among the Mothers are to be understood in this way; in those world-generating powers, the supreme reality is indeed freedom alone.

items.question: Why is the reality of willing, knowing, and acting worthy of worship?
premises: The worshippable reality consists of willing, knowing, and acting.
It is unlimited.
All directions of limitation are gathered within it.
items.inference: Because it is unbounded and contains all possible limitations, the triad of willing, knowing, and acting is supremely worshippable.
items.plain_english: This worshippable reality, consisting of willing, knowing, and acting, is worthy of worship because it is unlimited; even all directions of limitation are gathered within it.

items.question: Why does worshippability require a conceptual state that gathers many attributes?
premises: The non-conceptual does not attain worshippability here.
A single conceptual construction does not suffice where many attributes are present.
Therefore one attribute must gather in that many attributes.
items.inference: Worshippability arises not in bare non-conceptuality but in a unifying conceptual focus that comprehends many attributes.
items.plain_english: Here the non-conceptual does not attain worshippability, nor does a mere single concept where many attributes are involved; therefore the attribute that gathers in that many attributes is required.

items.question: What is the principle of supreme Bhairava worship taught in the Ḍāmara?
premises: That which draws in all attributes is established there as supreme.
All others stand in a lower position.
This is the principle of supreme Bhairava worship in the great rite of the revered Ḍāmara.
items.inference: Supreme worship centers on the unifying principle that comprehends all attributes, as taught in the Ḍāmara's great rite.
items.plain_english: That which draws in all attributes is established there as supreme, while all others stand lower; such is the principle of supreme Bhairava worship in the great rite of the revered Ḍāmara.

items.question: How should worship be performed in the external rite according to Śambhu's teaching?
premises: The glorious Śambhu himself, well pleased, taught this to me.
In the external rite, worship is to be performed.
It should be done in the triad of lotuses as well.
items.inference: Following Śambhu's direct teaching, external worship must be carried out upon the triad of lotuses.
items.plain_english: The glorious Śambhu himself, well pleased, taught this to me: in the external rite one should worship also in the triad of lotuses.

items.question: How is the retinue arranged in the directions according to the instructors' teaching?
premises: The retinue multitude is arranged ending with the weapon mantra.
This is stated in the teaching of the instructors.
The fivefold group of vidyā-limbs is placed in the directions of fire, Īśa, the demons, Vāyu, and the intermediate quarters.
items.inference: The instructors prescribe a directional installation of the retinue culminating in the weapon mantra and the five vidyā-limbs.
uncertainties: The exact mapping of the five directions is compressed; read as the specified quarters including intermediate ones.
items.plain_english: The teaching of the instructors is that the retinue multitude ends with the weapon mantra, and the fivefold group of vidyā-limbs is placed in the directions of Agni, Īśa, the demons, Vāyu, and the intermediate quarters.

items.question: Where are the limbs of Śakti and Śiva and the weapon and Locana mantras placed?
premises: The limbs of Śakti and the limbs of Śiva are placed likewise here.
Again in the pair, the weapon mantra should be placed in the four directions.
In the middle one should place the mantra called Locana.
items.inference: The ritual installation distributes Śakti and Śiva limbs, places the weapon mantra to the four directions, and centers Locana.
uncertainties: The phrase 'again in the pair' is terse and may refer to a paired ritual context from the surrounding passage.
items.plain_english: Here one should likewise place the limbs of Śakti and the limbs of Śiva; again in the pair, place the weapon mantra in the four directions, and in the middle place the mantra called Locana.

items.question: How are the mantra groups arranged on the petals and in further sets?
premises: On the eight petals a pair of octads beginning with Aghorā is placed according to its own tradition.
Likewise groups of twelve, six, and four are used.
These are arranged mixed, two by two.
items.inference: The rite layers octads, then sets of twelve, six, and four, distributing them in paired combinations according to tradition.
uncertainties: svayāmalam is read as 'according to its own tradition/Āmala source'.
items.plain_english: On the eight petals place a pair of octads beginning with Aghorā, according to its own tradition; likewise arrange groups of twelve, six, and four, mixed and distributed two by two.

items.question: How should the enclosing worship and the world guardians be arranged?
premises: Worship should be performed in every way as a doubled enclosure.
Then the world guardians should be worshipped.
They are placed with their weapons in their own ten directions in order.
items.inference: The rite proceeds by doubled concentric worship followed by sequential installation of the world guardians in all ten directions.
items.plain_english: One should worship in every way as a doubled enclosure; then, in order, worship the world guardians with their weapons in their own ten directions.

items.question: From what inner stance should the practitioner satisfy the host of deities?
premises: The practitioner abides in identity with the goddesses up to the trident.
Standing in that state, he offers the universe.
By this he should satisfy the host of deities.
items.inference: Satisfaction of the deities is accomplished by offering the universe while identified with the goddess-powers of the trident.
items.plain_english: Thus, abiding in identity with the goddesses up to the trident, standing here and offering the universe, one should satisfy the host of deities.

items.question: How should mantra recitation be performed after the offering?
premises: After that one should perform recitation.
Each mantra is recited ten times.
Because each is threefold in nature and yet non-different, this applies in all respects.
items.inference: Recitation proceeds mantra by mantra, ten times each, grounded in the mantras' simultaneous threefoldness and unity.
items.plain_english: Then one should perform recitation, ten times for each mantra; because each is threefold in nature and yet non-different, this holds in all respects.

items.question: How is the mantra circle visualized and used for inner oblation?
premises: The mantra circle is remembered like fire in the navel, heart, throat, palate, and upper center.
There the universe is present.
Burning it, one should accomplish the oblation.
items.inference: Internal recitation culminates in a fiery visualization of the mantra circle that consumes the universe as an inner offering.
uncertainties: jvahvan is read as a participial form related to burning (√jval).
items.plain_english: Remembering the mantra circle like fire in the navel, heart, throat, palate, and upper center, one should there burn the universe and accomplish the oblation.

items.question: Where should the teacher first apply the path of initiation when performing the rite?
premises: When the act of initiation is to be performed, the teacher chooses a path.
Desiring to perform initiation, he begins in the body.
At first he should primarily apply that path there.
items.inference: The initiation path selected by the teacher is first and foremost applied within the disciple's body.
items.plain_english: When the act of initiation is to be performed, by whichever path the teacher desires to carry it out, he should first and primarily apply that path in the body.
